correlates.name: Dilated Cardiomyopathy
correlates.presentation: Heart failure; the heart is visibly big.
correlates.pathophysiology: All four chambers dilate. The LV chamber diameter - and therefore the radius in Laplace - increases while the wall thins.

correlates.name: Heart Failure and Digoxin
correlates.presentation: Ejection fraction; on the Starling curve, an effective inotrope shifts the failing curve back toward normal.
correlates.pathophysiology: In heart failure the heart becomes weak from causes such as hypertension or myocardial infarction, and contractility is reduced (Slide 21).
correlates.treatment: Cardioactive glycosides such as digoxin inhibit the Na+/K+ ATPase (sodium pump), whose normal ATP-dependent job is K+ in and Na+ out against their electrochemical gradients.

correlates.name: Calcific Aortic Stenosis
correlates.presentation: A 73-year-old man in the ER with exertional dyspnea, syncope and chest pain. Poorly managed hypercholesterolemia and an 11-year history of hypertension.
correlates.pathophysiology: The obstructed aortic valve cannot open and close fully, so left ventricular pressure must climb very high to eject across it.
correlates.treatment: Aortic valve repair or replacement, depending on the patient's condition.

drugs.name: Digoxin
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits the myocyte Na+/K+ ATPase, so intracellular sodium rises, the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger slows, cytoplasmic calcium accumulates and more calcium binds troponin
drugs.indication: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, shifting a depressed Frank-Starling curve back to the left; also rate control in atrial fibrillation
drugs.adverseEffects: A narrow therapeutic window — hypokalemia leaves fewer K+ ions competing at the pump, so diuretics precipitate arrhythmia; verapamil raises levels by blocking P-glycoprotein

formulas.name: Ejection Fraction
formulas.equation: EF = (EDV - ESV) x 100 / EDV = SV x 100 / EDV
formulas.meaning: The fraction of the end-diastolic volume actually ejected — the standard non-invasive measure of systolic function, obtained by transthoracic echocardiography
formulas.normalValue: Normally 55-70%; a reduced value defines HFrEF

formulas.name: Fractional Shortening
formulas.meaning: The same idea as ejection fraction but measured from linear chamber dimensions rather than volumes
formulas.normalValue: An echocardiographic alternative when volumes are hard to trace

formulas.name: Ventricular Wall Stress
formulas.meaning: The primary determinant of myocardial oxygen consumption — dilation raises the radius and thinning lowers wall thickness, so both drive demand up
formulas.normalValue: An efficient heart has a small radius and an adequately thick wall; a big floppy ventricle is metabolically expensive

formulas.name: Frank-Starling Law
formulas.equation: Stroke volume rises as end-diastolic volume rises
formulas.meaning: Greater passive stretch produces greater force of contraction, so the ventricle ejects whatever extra volume returns to it — on the pressure-volume loop only EDV moves, not ESV
formulas.normalValue: The curve shifts up and left in exercise and with positive inotropes, and down and right in heart failure

formulas.name: Pressure-Volume Loop Landmarks
formulas.equation: EDV ~120 mL, ESV ~50 mL, stroke volume ~70 mL — the width of the loop
formulas.meaning: Traversed counterclockwise: filling, isovolumetric contraction, rapid and reduced ejection, then isovolumetric relaxation; the EDPVR describes passive stiffness and the ESPVR describes contractility
formulas.normalValue: A stiff hypertrophied ventricle steepens the EDPVR; a failing ventricle shifts the ESPVR right

formulas.name: Indicator Dilution Cardiac Output
formulas.equation: CO = (mg dye x 60) / (average concentration per mL x curve duration in seconds)
formulas.meaning: Cardiogreen injected into a large vein travels through the right heart, lungs and left heart, and the shape of the peripheral concentration curve reports the output
formulas.normalValue: A deeper, delayed and longer curve means a reduced cardiac output; recirculation makes the tail rise again

formulas.name: Heart Rate Ceiling for Cardiac Output
formulas.equation: Cardiac output rises with heart rate up to 180-200 bpm, then falls
formulas.meaning: Faster rates shorten diastole and cut stroke volume, but up to that ceiling the rate increase more than compensates; beyond it both stroke volume and output collapse
formulas.normalValue: Subendocardial left ventricle is perfused only during diastole, which is why tachycardia also starves the coronaries
